name: Navigate from hero to installation
description: Verifies the main page exposes the hero, terminal illustration and working installation destinations.
steps: Inspect the packaged and source installation options
expected: The hero is visible, Get started navigates to Install, the release link targets the RIKO GitHub Releases page, and clone commands use the real repository URL and root directory.

name: Mobile navigation and responsive cards
description: Checks the narrow layout remains readable without page-level horizontal overflow.
steps: Open the Menu control and follow a navigation link
Inspect feature cards, terminal illustration and screenshot slots
expected: Navigation collapses into a menu, menu links close the menu, the feature grid is one column, the terminal scrolls horizontally within its frame, and screenshot cards show the actual uploaded text-chat and voice-chat screenshot images with polished frames and no mockup placeholders.

name: Verify status roadmap and exact credits
description: Verifies roadmap items remain marked in progress and the requested credit lines are present verbatim.
expected: The roadmap displays 'Desktop GUI (GTK4) — in progress' and 'Growth mode and voice barge-in tuning — in progress'; both required credit lines match the supplied wording.

name: Copy repository-root installation commands
description: Verifies command blocks remain available on mobile and describe first-run setup accurately.
steps: Use a Copy button for a command block
Inspect setup notes for Windows and Linux
expected: Windows commands end with install.bat and run.bat; Linux commands end with bash install.sh and bash run.sh; notes explain internet-required model downloads, Debian/Ubuntu scope and the partial Kokoro download retry caveat.

name: Review privacy and requirements disclosures
description: Checks the page does not promise fully offline operation or overstate voice interruption.
expected: Hardware and memory estimates are shown with caveats, privacy copy states setup needs internet, and voice interruption is clearly labelled as a prototype without acoustic echo cancellation.
